observationsNotFindings: The AT-8 handling is the most careful thing in this artifact and it is worth the coordinator understanding why it matters. AT-8 is a requirement class in acceptanceTests but deliberately has no aggregate key in the fixtureMemberMap; instead it decomposes into 17 distinct AT-ARCHIVE-* members. A catalog that added an AT-8 map key would have created a fixture obligation the contract never defined, and one that collapsed the 17 into AT-8 would have hidden 16 of them. This does neither, and records both facts explicitly as noAggregateAt8MapKey and at8IsTheSetOfAtArchiveMembers.

The large integers are quotations, not thresholds, and the distinction is worth stating because it looks alarming at a glance. 8589934591 and 8589934592, 2097151 and 2097152, and 100 and 101 are USTAR field boundaries already embedded in live v14 member key names and require text, each appearing as an accept/refuse pair. The catalog carries no number that v14 does not, apart from required-now 26 and the verified member count 27.

Four members carry blocked-on-ride rather than a pass, riding DR-112, DR-110 and DR-102 through ID-DEP-P3 and ID-DEP-P4. Those rides are to rows that are not closed, so a substantial part of the AT surface cannot be executed even once fixtures exist. The catalog preserves that honestly rather than presenting the class as ready.

This is the largest and most quotation-dense catalog in the family - 8 classes, 27 members, roughly 150 quoted fields - and unlike the G09 and G10 catalogs its source offers rich per-member structure that it fully reproduces. A later fixture-authoring cycle inherits producer, expected outcome and ride for every member, which is the most complete handoff of any catalog I have reviewed in this sweep.

decision.scopeOfAccept: This ACCEPT is of at-named-corpus-catalog.v1 as a named catalog of the eight live v14 acceptance-test requirement classes and the twenty-seven live AT-* fixtureMemberMap members, at status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED binding NOTHING. It is not an application of v14, not an execution of G15, not a seal, not a SATISFIED of DR-120 or DR-103, and not a QUALIFIED. decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. Every claim in this catalog is mechanically checkable and every one checks. namedCorpusNotAuthored equals live v14 acceptanceTests.classes rendered as 'AT-N name' across all eight; the 27-key atFixtureMemberKeysInOrder equals the AT-prefixed keys of live conformanceReport.fixtureMemberMap.members in insertion order; the AT-ARCHIVE-* count of 17 and AT-* count of 27 both confirm by enumeration; and 135 member field comparisons plus 8 class quotations return 0 mismatches. One thing is worth flagging about my own process: my first extraction of the fixtureMemberMap looked like it refuted the ordered-key claim outright, because the map's entries live one level down under .members rather than at its root. That was my level error, and I checked the structure before drawing any conclusion. AT-8 is handled exactly right - it is a requirement class with no aggregate map key, decomposing instead into the 17 AT-ARCHIVE-* members, and the catalog records both facts rather than collapsing or inventing. The large integers are the other thing that looks alarming and is not: 8589934591, 2097151, 100, 101 and their pairs are USTAR field boundaries already in live v14, and the only numbers absent from v14 are required-now 26 and the member count 27 that I verified by enumeration. Four members correctly hold blocked-on-ride against DR-112, DR-110 and DR-102 rather than being softened into passes. The v14 source pin is dual-reviewed and recorded at D-108, and no pin is mine. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
